Subject: Redwood private deployment — pricing clarification and schedule

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about the latency and cost profile. Procurement asked me to get a clear line on two items before we issue an LOI: 1) how the platform fee is amortized if we do an 18-month pilot before full rollout, and 2) the operator/seat license model vs a per-GPU node charge for our multi-datacenter setup (we're planning 3 sites).

Specific asks:
- Show a 0–18 month amortization option for the platform fee and the monthly vs upfront effect on ARR.
- If we move operator licenses to a usage floor (for burst nodes) what discounts do you apply at 250 / 500 / 1,000 node-months?
- We need a timeline for delivery: pilot acceptance criteria, staggered site activation (canary -> site 2 -> site 3), and an SRE retainer option for 24x7 on-call during rollout.

Also, our legal team will want a short clause around rollback and data handling — can you confirm whether escrow(artifact) and audit logs retention are supported in your Private deployment offering?

Would be great to have a single spreadsheet with permutations we can circulate internally. Can you share by EOD Wednesday (PST)?

Thanks,
Sally
Head of Platform Operations
OpsHealth

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood private deployment — pricing clarification and schedule

Sally — thanks for the clear list.

High-level answers first, spreadsheet attached (redwood-privdeploy-pricing-v3.xlsx) with three commercialization paths: (A) upfront platform fee + lower node pricing, (B) amortized platform fee over 18 months + medium node pricing, (C) fully metered (no upfront) with an SRE retainer add-on. Quick bullets:
- Amortization: we can amortize the platform fee over 12 or 18 months; amortizing over 18 months raises monthly cash by ~18% vs 12-month amortization but lowers initial capex. See tab "Amortized Options" for per-month P&L impact and ARR equivalence.
- Operator vs node: operator licenses are priced per-seat for the SRE/ops team (recommended 2 seats per site) + per-GPU site license. For burst nodes we offer a tiered usage rebate: 250 node-months = 8% rebate, 500 = 12%, 1,000+ = 18% — these assume a 12–24 month commit.
- Pilot & rollout: propose an 8-week pilot (canary site) with defined acceptance criteria (latency, failover, KV cache hitrate, integration smoke tests). Site activation schedule in the sheet (canary week 0–8, site 2 week 9–14, site 3 week 15–20).
- SRE retainer: options at $12k/month (business-hours), $28k/month (24x7 L2 on-call + 2 on-call engineers), or a blended $18k/month for limited-hour coverage.
- Escrow & audit: we support model+artifact escrow and configurable audit-log retention (30/90/365 days). We'll provide standard language for rollback and data-handling; legal has accepted similar clauses previously.

Action: I'm looping in Marissa for discounts/credits and David for SRE scope. Kimberly — could you confirm any constraints on amortizing the platform fee for public sector accounting?

Deliverable: spreadsheet attached + SOW draft (opshealth-multi-site-sow-draft.docx). We'll get a DocuSign-ready term-sheet once we lock the discount matrix.

Best,
Monica Patel
Commercial Lead — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood private deployment — pricing clarification and schedule

All — quick pricing notes and a recommended discount path for OpsHealth. I reviewed Monica's sheet and ran a sensitivity on operator-seat vs per-GPU economics. My recommended approach to preserve margin while being competitive:

1) Hybrid anchor: charge a 40% upfront platform fee (can be amortized) + tiered node pricing. Anchor prevents churn while giving immediate coverage.
2) Usage rebate ladder (applies to node consumption only): 250 node-months -> 7% rebate (intro), 500 -> 11%, 1,000+ -> 17%. Keep slightly below our standard list to give negotiation room.
3) Operator license transition: offer a one-time 50% discount on operator seats for the pilot period only (to reduce OpEx friction) and revert to standard pricing on full rollout. This addresses their ask about operator-seat costs.
4) SRE retainer: propose the blended $18k/month for pilot + a ramp to $28k after full activation. Include a 30-day termination with 60-day wind-down for retainer.

Open question for David/SRE: is the blended retainer feasible operationally for 3-site staggered go-live? If not, we'll need to keep the 24x7 rate.

Also — recommend a small implementation-credit if they sign within 30 days: a $25k implementation credit applied to first invoice. This helps Procurement get signoff.

If legal wants escrow language, we typically add a 12-month escrow window + audit log retention options as Monica flagged.

Marissa
VP, Commercials
Redwood Inference

If you can confirm the three items above in the SOW and provide a DocuSign-ready term sheet by Friday, procurement will circulate a PO within two business days of DocuSign execution.
